## AI reader

### ai-reader:measure

Read the files of a directory with the AI reader and write one JSON line per file.

Reads every PDF, PNG and JPEG file of a directory with the AI reader and writes one JSON line per
file, to the standard output or to the file of --output. Run it by hand to measure how well the
reader and a model do on your own documents, whatever the trigger setting. Each file is sent to the
AI provider and may cost money. The files stay where they are, nothing is stored in Foresi, and the
API key never reaches the output. It exits with 1 when the AI reader is not set up
(AI_READER_PROVIDER and AI_READER_API_KEY), and with 2 when the directory or the output file is not
usable.

```
bin/console ai-reader:measure /path/to/documents --output=measure.jsonl
```

```
bin/console ai-reader:measure [options] [--] <directory>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `directory` | yes |  | The directory with the PDF, PNG and JPEG files to read. |

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--model` | required |  | Read with this model instead of the one in AI_READER_MODEL. |
| `--output` | required |  | Write the lines to this file instead of the standard output. |

## Cash flow

### cashflow:pairing:backfill

Pair the documents of the last 13 months with planned occurrences.

Pairs the documents dated in the last 13 months with planned occurrences, as if each had just been
recorded. Run it once after installing Cash flow next to existing documents. It writes pairings,
leaves a pairing a person already decided as it is, and prints the number of pairings per state.
It is idempotent: a second run changes nothing.

```
bin/console cashflow:pairing:backfill
```

## Events

### app:events

List the contract events of the installed modules, or check them.

Lists the contract events of the installed modules with their version, module and facts. Run it
by hand to see which events a module publishes. With --check it prints what is wrong with the events
and exits with 1; CI runs it (composer events:check). It is read-only and safe to repeat. Use
--format=json for scripts.

```
bin/console app:events [options]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--format` | required | `'table'` | table or json. |
| `--check` | none |  | Print the problems and exit 1 when there are any. |

## Exchange rate

### app:exchange-rate:fetch

Fetch and store the exchange rates valid on a date (default today).

Fetches the exchange rates valid on a date from a rate source and stores them. The schedule does
this every day for the source the firm converts at, so run the command by hand only to fill a missed
date, to check the connection, or to fill another installed source before the firm switches to it.
It writes rates only and is safe to repeat. It exits with 1 when the source gives no usable answer
and stores nothing, and with 2 when the date or the source name is invalid.

```
bin/console app:exchange-rate:fetch 2026-11-06 --source=ecb
```

```
bin/console app:exchange-rate:fetch [options] [--] [<date>]
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | no |  | The date as YYYY-MM-DD; today when omitted. |

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--source` | required |  | The name of an installed source, such as cnb or ecb; the one the firm converts at when omitted. |

## Identity

### app:api-token:issue

Issue a personal API token for a user.

Issues a personal API token for an existing user who is the owner or a team member. Run it by hand
when someone needs the REST API or the MCP server; the token acts as that person with the scopes you
give. At least one --scope is required; repeat the option for more. The command writes one token.
The secret is printed once and stored nowhere, so copy it from the output. Running it again issues
another token. It exits with 1 when the user is unknown or the request is refused, and with 2 for
invalid input.

```
bin/console app:api-token:issue owner@example.com --name="Reporting" --days=90 --scope=read
```

```
bin/console app:api-token:issue [options] [--] <email>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | yes |  | E-mail address of the user. |

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--name` | required |  | What the token is for, 1 to 80 characters. |
| `--days` | required | `90` | Days until it expires: 30, 90 or 365. |
| `--scope` | required, repeatable |  | read, write, or a resource such as contacts:read or contacts:write; repeat for more. |

### app:api-token:list

List personal API tokens.

Lists the personal API tokens of the instance with their user, scopes, expiry, last use and state.
Run it by hand to see who holds a token and whether it is still used, for example before revoking
one. It is read-only and safe to repeat. Only the last four characters of each token are known, so
no secret is printed.

```
bin/console app:api-token:list
```

### app:api-token:revoke

Revoke a personal API token.

Revokes a personal API token of any user, so it stops working at once. Run it by hand when a token
leaked or is no longer needed; app:api-token:list shows the ids. It changes the one token and
nothing else. Revoking a token again is harmless. It exits with 1 when no token has the id.

```
bin/console app:api-token:revoke <token-id>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `token-id` | yes |  | Id of the token. |

### app:user:create

Create a user and their membership.

Creates a person who can sign in, together with their membership, in one transaction. Run it once
after installation to create the first owner, or later to add a user without an invitation. It asks
for a display name and a password of at least 12 characters.
A guest must represent an existing contact, so pass --contact with its id.
It writes one user and one membership. It is not safe to repeat: a second run for the same e-mail
address fails with exit code 1 and changes nothing.

```
bin/console app:user:create owner@example.com owner
```

```
bin/console app:user:create [options] [--] <email> <role>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | yes |  | E-mail address, used to sign in. |
| `role` | yes |  | owner, member or guest. |

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--contact` | required |  | Id of the contact the user represents; required for a guest. |

### app:user:reset-2fa

Turn off the two-factor sign-in of a user, who sets it up again on the next sign-in.

Turns off the two-factor sign-in of a user and forgets their trusted browsers. Run it by hand when
the person lost their authenticator and recovery codes. They set up two-factor sign-in again on the
next sign-in. The reset is written to the log. It is safe to repeat. It exits with 1 when no user
has the e-mail address.

```
bin/console app:user:reset-2fa owner@example.com
```

```
bin/console app:user:reset-2fa <email>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | yes |  | E-mail address of the user. |

## Import

### app:import:health

Fail imports that stopped moving and start the imports queued behind them.

Fails imports that stopped moving and starts the imports queued behind them. An import in
Reading, Checking, Running or Undoing that changed neither state nor counters for four hours is
marked Failed, and every target with queued imports and none running then starts its oldest queued
import. Run it from cron every 15 minutes. It changes imports of the whole instance, it does not
re-send lost messages, and a failed import can be uploaded again. It is safe to repeat; a release
that failed is repaired by the next run. It exits with 1 when an import could not be failed or a
queue not released.

```
bin/console app:import:health
```

### app:import:purge

Delete the files and staged rows of imports that ended more than 30 days ago.

Deletes the source file, the staged rows and the staged missing records of imports that ended
more than 30 days ago. Imports that never ended and are older than 30 days (waiting for the user)
are cancelled first. The import record and its counters stay, and an import can no longer be undone
once purged. Run it from cron once a day. It works on the whole instance and is safe to repeat.

```
bin/console app:import:purge
```

## Instance

### app:health

Check the database, worker, schedule, disk and system mail.

Runs the checks of /health from the shell and prints them as a table: database, worker, schedule,
disk and system mail. Run it from cron or a monitoring agent, or by hand to see why /health reports
a problem. It is read-only and safe to repeat. It exits with 1 when the installation is down and
with 0 otherwise, including when it is only degraded.

```
bin/console app:health
```

## Invoicing

### app:invoice:revoke-link

End the links of a sent document for good.

Ends both links of one send of a document for good. Run it by hand when a link went to a wrong
address, because a delivered invoice cannot go to the trash. The change goes through the send, so
the audit log records it. Sending the document again gives a new link. It is safe to repeat. It
exits with 1 when no send has the id.

```
bin/console app:invoice:revoke-link
```

```
bin/console app:invoice:revoke-link <sendId>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sendId` | yes |  | The id of the send, as the send log shows it. |

## Margin

### margin:recalculate

Count the cost shares of every recorded document again.

Counts the cost shares of every document the cost sources know about, so the documents recorded
before Margin was installed get theirs. Run it once after installing Margin next to existing
documents, or to rebuild the shares after a mapping changed. It replaces the shares of each document
with what its mapping says now and prints the number of documents and shares. It is idempotent: a
second run changes nothing.

```
bin/console margin:recalculate
```

## Shared

### app:migrations:owners

Check that every table of the database is created by the migrations of one installed module.

Checks that every table of the database is created by the migrations of exactly one installed
module. Run it after the migrations, in CI and after installing or removing a module. On the full
application it finds a table with no owner; on a subset of modules it finds a table of a module that
is not installed. It is read-only and safe to repeat. It exits with 1 and prints the problems when a
table has no owner. Use --list to print every table with its module.

```
bin/console app:migrations:owners [options]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--list` | none |  | Also list each table with its module. |

### app:migrations:rebase

Move a database from the global migration history onto the module baselines, without DDL.

Moves a database from the old global migration history onto the baselines of the modules. It
replaces the rows of the executed versions only and changes no table. Run it once, from the live
release, on an existing database that the deploy left alone; take a backup first
(ops/backup.sh --tag pre-rebase). It refuses and changes nothing when a version is missing or the
schema is out of sync. A database already on the baselines needs nothing and exits with 0.

With --check it changes nothing and reports the state by its exit code: 0 when there is nothing to
rebase (a new database, or one already on the baselines), 2 when the database is on the global
history, 1 otherwise. ops/deploy.sh uses this.

```
bin/console app:migrations:rebase [options]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--check` | none |  | Only tell the state: exit 0 with nothing to rebase, 2 when a rebase is due, 1 otherwise. |

### app:modules

List the installed modules, their dependencies, their integrations and the problems of the module graph.

Lists the installed modules with their kind, package, required and optional dependencies and
scopes, then the integrations between modules and the problems of the module graph. Run it by hand
to see what is installed and which integrations are loaded. It is read-only and safe to repeat. It
exits with 1 when a problem is not listed in extra.foresi.accepted-problems of the root
composer.json. Use --format=json for scripts.

```
bin/console app:modules [options]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--format` | required | `'table'` | table or json. |

### app:modules:check

Check that the installed modules are written for the module API of this Foresi, or of the version given.

Checks that every installed module is written for the module API this Foresi provides, or for the
version given with --api. Run it in CI for a module, and before an upgrade with the version the
upgrade brings. The deploy runs it after composer install and before the migrations, so an
incompatible module never touches the database. It is read-only and safe to repeat. It exits with 1
and names each module that does not fit, and with 2 when --api is not a version.

```
bin/console app:modules:check --api=2.0
```

```
bin/console app:modules:check [options]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--api` | required | `'1.10.0'` | The module API version to check against, such as 2.0; the one this Foresi provides when left out. |

### app:modules:deptrac

Generate the module-level Deptrac configuration from the module manifests.

Writes deptrac.modules.yaml, the module-level Deptrac configuration, from the module manifests.
Run it when a module or a dependency between modules changed, then commit the file. With --check it
writes nothing and compares only; CI runs it (composer modules:check) and exits with 1 when the file
differs from the manifests. Writing is safe to repeat. It exits with 1 when the file cannot be
written.

```
bin/console app:modules:deptrac [options]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--check` | none |  | Only compare the file with the manifests; fail when it differs. |
| `--file` | required |  | The file to write or compare; deptrac.modules.yaml of the project when left out. |

### app:ops:test-alert

Log one error to check the error mail to the operator.

Logs one error, to check that it reaches the log file and the operator's mailbox. Run it after
setting OPERATOR_EMAIL and OPERATOR_MAILER_DSN. The message carries the time, so every run is a
distinct message and passes the hourly deduplication of error mails. It writes only a log line, and
it always exits with 0; check the mailbox for the result.

```
bin/console app:ops:test-alert
```

### app:ops:test-mail

Send a test system mail to check the system mailer.

Queues one test mail through the system mailer, to check SYSTEM_MAILER_DSN and SYSTEM_MAIL_FROM.
Run it after setting up or changing the system mail. It sends nothing itself: the worker sends the
queued mail, so a worker must run, and the mail arrives only when the transport works. Each run
queues one more mail. It exits with 1 when the system mailer is not set up or the address is
invalid.

```
bin/console app:ops:test-mail owner@example.com
```

```
bin/console app:ops:test-mail <to>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `to` | yes |  | The address to send the test mail to. |

### app:views:sync

Store the default views of the installed modules, leaving edited and hidden ones alone.

Stores the default views that the installed modules ship. It adds missing views and brings views
that nobody edited or hid up to what the module now declares. A view that someone changed or hid
stays as it is. The deploy runs it after the migrations, and the install runs it too; run it by hand
after adding a module. It is safe to repeat: a second run changes nothing.

```
bin/console app:views:sync
```
